items.name: Entry points

Autonomous path: scaler3::controller -> execute_split_fenced / resume_fenced; only started by scaler3::start (src/bootstrap.rs:761), never in HTTP rigs.
items.detail: The function returns true only if Phase B published in this call. If Phase A declines, it still calls resume_incarnation (lines 302-304) to finish a transition someone else started. It takes no locks beyond the registry CAS; everything runs as the caller's await chain.

items.name: Phase A: persist intent (registry CAS)
items.where: topology.rs:244-300 (registry.mutate_incarnation(sref, expect_epoch, ...))
items.detail:
The CAS declines if the stream is deleted, forked or has forks, is sealed or sealing, already has map.pending, or if the segment is missing, not live, or split_at falls outside (lo, hi). Otherwise it builds the implicit map (SegmentMap::initial) and sets map.pending = {kind:'split', segs:[seg_id], split_at, started_ms, seal_gen}; it also bumps map.version and d.seal_gen_counter (seal_gen = counter).
APPEND AT THIS MOMENT: the parent is still is_live() (segmap.rs:51; the intent lives only in map.pending), and DescriptorView resolve_segment (registry.rs:737-790) ignores pending, so the append routes to parent seg 0: identity storage_hash(), parent route. It commits normally on the parent's engine at an offset below the future frozen offset. Answer: 200/204.
PAUSE TODAY: none dedicated. Coarse options: FaultStore::hold_class(StoreOp::Put, ObjClass::Other, 1) (fault_store.rs:361) parks the first 'Other' PUT anywhere in the rig, which includes descriptor writes but also any other registry or billing put. registry.fail_next_put(name) (registry.rs:1290) only forces a CAS conflict and retry; it does not pause. A test-only hook would go in resume_incarnation right after the pending read and before seal_segment_identity (topology.rs:427), e.g. Fp::ScalerBeforeSeal keyed by desc.name, mirroring pause_scaler_before_publish.

items.name: Resume + parent seal (close op to the parent's committer)
items.where: topology.rs:403-433 resume_incarnation (invalidate, get, epoch fence, pending clone), 428 seal_segment_identity (42-86) -> close_segment_on_engine (89-125: engine.try_close(CloseReq{hash: parent identity, generation: seal_gen})) or relay_segment_close (133-215, POST /v1/internal/segment-close, receiver http.rs:2983). Committer side: src/shard/transaction/maintenance.rs:110-136 (close sets fields.closed, acks frozen next_offset); reply released at the durability barrier.
items.detail:
The engine is resolved with Adoption::Internal. NotOwner: the close is relayed to the owner, following one redirect; a second 409 returns None. Any other ResolveError, enqueue failure (queue full or closed), or refused or dropped reply returns None, and the resume returns false with the intent still pending. It is then resumed by the next reader, by an append's closure path, or by the scaler.
APPEND AT THIS MOMENT (routes to the parent, still live):
(a) Enqueued or staged before the close in the committer queue: it commits in the parent below frozen. 200/204.
(b) Staged after the close: transaction/append.rs:71-96 answers AppendErr::Closed{next}. from_commit makes it StreamClosed with engine_closed_segment=Some(0). execute_prepared (append.rs:167-190) then calls closure_is_current (append.rs:198-239): invalidate + get. With pending set, it calls lifecycle.topology.schedule(desc), which is request_work and coalesces per (stream, epoch, Topology), and waits on ticket.wait() (at most JOB_TIMEOUT 10 s, request_work.rs:14,56-70). It returns Ok(false), then sleeps 10/20/30 ms, calls prepare() to refresh, and retries. After 4 attempts it answers 503 segment_transition with retry-after 1. A ticket error or failed refresh also gives 503 segment_transition.
(c) The committed group's write fails: every op in the group, the close and co-grouped appends alike, gets AppendErr::Internal (transaction/finalize.rs:196 -> mod.rs:186-188). That is 500 append_failed on the product surface, and the seal returns None. This is item 47 when the error is slatedb Closed or Fenced.
(d) Engine closed before enqueue: try_enqueue Err gives 429 overloaded 'append queue full' with no Retry-After (submit.rs:79-84; D1).
(e) Queued when the engine closes: committer_loop (shard.rs:2449-2485) or CommitTransaction::run (mod.rs:52-55) answers Moved, which is 503 shard_moving with retry-after 1.
PAUSES TODAY:
- engine.test_hold_commit() (shard.rs:2555; gate at 2495): the committer takes one op, then parks until the guard drops, then drains the queue into ONE group. This gives deterministic ordering of close vs appends. Use engine.appends_enqueued() (2563) as the entered-proof; it counts appends and closes.
- failpoints park_append_before_enqueue(name) (site append.rs:349, after route::resolve_segment at 302 and before submit's engine resolve and enqueue): parks every non-close append of that name, including retries.
- engine.test_hold_dispatch() (shard.rs:2952): writes applied, replies withheld.
- FaultStore hold_class(Put, Wal, 1): durability held (see request_topology_debt.rs:74).
- engine.fail_next_group_for(identity) (shard.rs:2656): the next group containing that identity fails as Internal('failpoint: group write failed').
NOT usable here: park_close_before_enqueue, because its site append.rs:351 is only on the append-surface close path and the split's seal bypasses execute_once. completion_pause (NoWrite/Written/Durable, finalize.rs:15,192; shard.rs:2985) is private to shard::retirement_tests (fn pause_completion) and needs a pub(crate) accessor for DST use.

items.name: Seal-to-publication gap (ScalerBeforePublish)
items.where: topology.rs:435 (split) and 567 (merge): crate::failpoints::pause_scaler_before_publish(&desc.name); registry in src/failpoints.rs (Fp::ScalerBeforePublish, arm/release/parked per (point, name))
items.detail:
The parent identity is durably closed and map.pending is still set; the parent's SegmentDesc is still live in the map.
APPEND AT THIS MOMENT: it routes to the parent and gets Closed, so closure_is_current schedules a request_work resume. That resume also parks at the same per-name failpoint ('every resume of the NAMED stream parks'), so the append blocks until the failpoint is released or the 10 s job deadline passes; a timeout gives 503 segment_transition (retryable). Nothing can commit in this window. A request_work resume that runs but returns false still reports Ok(()), so the retry loop re-meets Closed and ends in 503 segment_transition.
EXISTING RIG: fixture_http.rs:566 rig_in_seal_gap(stream, per_key) arms the failpoint, spawns execute_split, and polls until the parent handle's durable.closed is set and the descriptor shows pending with one segment. It returns (state, addr, FailpointGuard, JoinHandle). FailpointGuard (fixture_failpoints.rs:28) releases on drop, and await_published (fixture_http.rs:669) waits for publication. parked(Fp::ScalerBeforePublish, name) gives the entered-proof.

items.name: Phase B: publish successors + clear intent (registry CAS)
items.where: topology.rs:445-535 (mutate_incarnation fenced on desc.stream_epoch) -> segmap.rs:300-355 SegmentMap::split; post-publish topology.rs:540-545 (SEGMENT_SPLITS++, scaler.retire_segments at scaler3.rs:596 = sketches only, registry.invalidate)
items.detail:
The CAS declines, keeping the intent, if the stream is deleted, sealed or sealing, the low route is missing, pending no longer equals p ('someone else already completed it'), next_seg_id overflows, or map.split errors. low_route is the parent's route, so it is the same engine. high_route is RouteHash::for_child(stream, child_id, salt), salted until shard_for_hash differs from the parent prefix. split() sets the parent's sealed_ms and sealed_next_offset = frozen and successors = [a, b], pushes two live children, and sets pending = None.
APPEND AT THIS MOMENT: with a fresh descriptor it routes to the child whose range holds the key point. With a stale pre-publish descriptor in this instance's cache it routes to the parent, gets Closed, then closure_is_current refreshes: no pending, and resolve now gives a child id different from attempted, so it returns false and the retry lands on the child. This is pinned by topology_scaling.rs:686 an_append_routed_by_a_pre_split_descriptor_lands_on_the_child, which uses registry.test_poison_cache at registry/cache.rs:279. The registry cache is generation-fenced (registry/cache.rs header and lines 208-215), so a get in flight across the CAS cannot put the stale descriptor back into the cache.
PAUSE TODAY: none after the CAS. A test-only hook would go inside `if published {` before st.registry.invalidate (topology.rs:540). A coarse alternative is FaultStore hold on Put/Other with max_parked 1.

items.name: Post-publication first use of the children (where the capacity-test 500 must have happened)
items.where: append.rs:302 route::resolve_segment -> submit.rs:17-24 shards.resolve(child route, Adoption::External) -> shard_directory.rs:238-298 -> sharddir.rs:454-635 get_or_open; engine side shard.rs:2320-2360 stream_handle (db.get tail) and transaction/prepare.rs:53-84 billing_rows (load_billing_meta); transaction/mod.rs:58-66, 152-157
items.detail:
The low child is a fresh identity on the parent's engine. The high child is a fresh identity on a different prefix, whose engine opens on first resolve.
Resolve outcomes and answers:
- Ready: proceeds.
- In-flight open longer than open_wait: Wait{shard_opening, retry 3} (503).
- Holdoff: Wait{shard_moving} (503).
- Opener error or deadline: Failed -> ResolveError::OpenFailed -> AppendCode::ShardOpen, FailureClass::Internal -> 500 append_failed.
In the committer, the first group per new identity reads the billing row and loads the tail handle. Either read failing rejects the whole group (or the op) with AppendErr::Internal (500). producer_lineage names the sealed parent; its chain loads run only with producer or seq headers, which the blast does not send.
PAUSES TODAY:
- sharddir GatePark via state.shards.gate_for_tests().test_park().arm(prefix) (sharddir.rs:302-365; used at runtime_retirement.rs:270). It is a blocking std condvar held inside the gate state.
- HttpRigOptions.open_park (fixture_http.rs:28-31, site 281-283): a rig-wide mutex before maintenance restoration, affecting every prefix.
There is no per-identity hook on the first stream_handle or billing load; one would go in ShardEngine::stream_handle's miss path (shard.rs:2330) or in CommitTransaction::stage (mod.rs:150).

items.name: Handle retirement / old-owner engine close: not part of a split
items.where: shard.rs:2382-2415 evict_idle_handles (ticker at 1709-1711, default handle_idle_evict 600 s at 1070); shard_directory.rs:440 retire (callers: 264 OwnershipMoved on resolve, 391 Shutdown, fleet.rs:836/1043, billing.rs:1848 SweepEviction); shard.rs:1855-1900 begin_close
items.detail:
The split never retires a StreamHandle or closes an engine. The parent's handle stays resident with closed=true until idle eviction; a reload reads the persisted closed tail, so the behaviour is unchanged. Engine closure comes only from directory retirement (ownership move, fleet eviction, sweep eviction, shutdown) or from the engine closing itself (ShardCloseNotifier). None of these runs in HTTP rigs before engine_shutdown.
begin_close retires stranded in-flight groups with Moved (503 shard_moving). A db write racing the store close or fence returns slatedb Closed or Fenced. That error is flattened to Internal (500) at finalize.rs:196, mod.rs:152-157 and prepare.rs:82: this is item 47 (plan D2).
To build a red test: FaultStore.hold_class(Put, Wal, 1) or engine.test_hold_commit, then state.shards.retire(prefix, ...) or engine.begin_close(), then release. request_topology_debt.rs:74-110 already shows 'hold WAL put + shutdown while the close is durability-ambiguous'.

items.name: How post_split_throughput_scales drives the split (no traffic at the boundary)
items.where: src/dst/tests/topology_scaling.rs:296-445 (blast_keys 21-50, blast_client 53-81, KeyedAppender::post 105-139)
items.detail:
Setup: 4 prefixes; wal_group_commit false (disables only the flush pump; groups still batch); 8 per-segment admission slots; holds gap_lock.
Sequence:
1. Warm-up, then three 2.5 s windows of 48 keep-alive clients on keys ga..gh. blast_keys sets stop and awaits every task, so no request is in flight when it returns.
2. execute_split(seg 0 at 0x8000..) is awaited: Phase A, seal, Phase B.
3. The test calls invalidate + get and resolves both child routes with engine_for_scaler (http/test_support.rs:43-48, Adoption::Internal), which opens the high child's engine.
4. Warm-up blast of 0.5 s, then four 2.5 s windows.
blast_client accepts only 200, 204, 503 and 429 (retried after 1 ms). Any other status panics the client task with 'append during capacity run: {status}'; the panic surfaces at t.await.unwrap(). The response body is read but discarded, so the 500's code and message were never captured.
Conclusion: the 500 answered an append issued after publication, with both child engines open. The reviewer's split-boundary windows (old-owner submission, sealing, publication, retirement, retry) had zero traffic in this test.

paths.summary:
Read-only analysis of slate at d4d631df (nothing built, run or edited).

1) The premise is probably wrong: the 500 most likely came before execute_split ran.
- The failing run (scratchpad/gate-b12.txt.capacity.log) finished in 8.63 s.
- Scripted sleeps up to the end of the post-split warm-up add up to 0.5 + 3×2.5 + 0.5 = 8.5 s.
- Every store op in this rig has a real 20 ms latency, including the registry. The split, the child-prefix open and the stream create together need at least nine sequential store ops, so at least 0.18 s. The post-split warm-up therefore cannot end before about 8.72 s.
- Passing runs of the same, unchanged test structure take 19.87–20.02 s: 18.5 s of sleeps plus about 1.45 s of overhead.
- 8.63 s fits the THIRD PRE-SPLIT measurement window (the `before` loop, topology_scaling.rs:363). The panic lines (:71, :45) are the same for every window, so "right after the split" came only from reading the wall time.
- In that window engine P served one segment to 48 clients. No transition, no engine open, close or fence, and no descriptor change was in progress. Item 47 (via fence) and child-shard OpenFailed are not reachable there.

2) The only mechanism I found that yields an `Internal` in steady state in this rig is an absorber double-retirement. It rejects a whole commit group with "maintenance accounting diverged".
- A dirty-index rescan runs every 120 absorber ticks, which is 2.4 s at the rig's 20 ms tick, so each 2.5 s window contains exactly one rescan.
- If the rescan runs while an AbsorbedBatch has been submitted but not yet applied, it treats the batch's mark as stranded and rolls it back.
- The next gather then starts from the stale durable boundary. It re-reports bytes the committer is about to retire, and the committer retires them a second time because the new batch still advances the boundary.
- If the per-stream ledger underflows, every append in that group gets AppendErr::Internal: raw surface 500 `internal`, product 500 `append_failed` with retryable:false.
- Those appends were not committed; the group is rejected before the write.
- It is one-shot: the raised mark prevents a repeat, and the ledger then over-counts forever (a phantom backlog). That matches "one 500, never reproduced".
- The same mechanism also plausibly explains the undiagnosed 2/40 "split executes" failures under CPU load: a diverging batch in the same group as the seal's CloseReq. The status note's "seal misses its deadline" has no code basis; that path has no deadline and the queue holds 65,536.

3) Every other 500 path is listed below with file:line, trigger, split-phase reachability and commit ambiguity. None is reachable in the observed window. A split never retires the parent's engine: the low child reuses its route and only the high child gets a new prefix. So during a single-instance split there is no "old engine retiring", and sealing is the only phase that is exposed, through its group.

4) Incidental, not a 500: producer and Stream-Seq lineage lookups only read the local engine's DB. A high child on a different prefix cannot see its parent's rows, so a producer retry that committed on the parent is accepted again. No test covers this across two engines.

5) How to confirm:
- Run with DST_DRAIN_TRACE. It prints GATHER from/upto and ADVANCE prev/upto; an ADVANCE whose gather started below prev is the overlap.
- A body-printing harness on the product surface cannot tell Internal causes apart, because the product body hides the message. Use the raw surface's body or a tracing subscriber instead.
- Red test with controlled pauses: hold P's commit gate after a gather submits, force seed_from_dirty_index, append, gather again, enqueue an append, release. The append should get Internal.

Lower bounds on the remaining work: stream create is at least 2 ops; execute_split is at least Phase A get+put, a resume get, the seal's durable ack (one WAL PUT) and Phase B get+put; the test's own registry get is one more; the child-prefix Db open is at least 2 ops. Passing runs of the same, unchanged structure (last edited 85017d84, before the gate) take 19.87–20.02 s, i.e. 18.5 s of sleeps plus about 1.45 s of overhead. 8.63 s equals 8.0 s plus about 0.6 s of setup and join tails, which fits the THIRD `before` window. items.name: RANK 1 — Absorber double-retires a range; the committer rejects the whole group with 'maintenance accounting diverged' (Internal → 500)
items.where: src/history/worker.rs:47,82-88 (rescan every 120 ticks; rig tick 20 ms per fixture_http.rs:309-315, so 2.4 s; tokio interval default Burst); src/history/gather.rs:283 + 323-352 (roll_back_stranded_mark), 475-500 (plan_read: from = max(mark, durable.absorbed)), 586-591 (advance = (hash, last+1, chunk_raw), no `from`), 661-663 (send, then raise mark); src/shard.rs:2108-2150 (dirty scan reads applied state); src/shard/transaction/maintenance.rs:169-202 (retires full `bytes` whenever upto > prev_absorbed; underflow at :187-194); src/shard/transaction/finalize.rs:5-8 → mod.rs:186-188 (AppendErr::Internal on every reply in the group) → application/append/contract.rs:276 → http.rs:27 (500) / product.rs:2421 ('append_failed', retryable:false)
items.detail:
Sequence:
1. Gather G1 sends an AbsorbedBatch covering [a0..n1) and raises the mark to n1.
2. The next tick is a rescan tick. It can fire immediately, because a gather with 20 ms history write and flush overruns the tick and Burst catches up. Its dirty-row read happens before the committer applied G1, so it sees absorbed = a0 < mark and drops the mark as 'stranded'. The comment at gather.rs:330-334 calls re-submission harmless, which is false once new data makes it an advancing boundary.
3. The same tick's gather G2 plans from handle.durable.absorbed. That is still a0, because G1 is not durable yet (WAL flush is 5 ms plus a 20 ms PUT). G2 submits bytes[a0..n2).
4. The committer applies G1 (absorbed = n1, ledger minus bytes[a0..n1)), then G2. Since n2 > n1, it retires bytes[a0..n2) — the first part a second time.
5. If bytes[a0..n1) exceeds the unabsorbed tail beyond n2, checked_sub fails and the entire commit group is rejected. That hits every co-grouped append on the engine, plus closes and queue ops.

Consequences:
- Not committed: the group is rejected before db.write, yet it is reported as a non-definitive 500 that the SDK will not retry.
- One-shot: the mark raised at :663 makes the next gather skip the rejected range, so it doesn't repeat. The tail ledger and the shard's unabsorbed_frame_bytes then over-count forever, a phantom backlog that never returns to 0. Checking for that is a way to detect the event after the fact.
- If there is no immediate underflow, the ledger silently under-counts and the divergence fires later, e.g. at a split parent's final drain.

Phase reachability:
- Steady state on any hot stream; each 2.5 s window on P contains exactly one rescan. This fits the observation.
- Sealing: the parent's final drain coincides with the seal. A diverging batch co-grouped with the CloseReq makes the close answer Internal (application/topology.rs:113-116), the seal returns None and execute_split returns false. That plausibly explains the 2/40 'split executes' failures under CPU load. The 'seal deadline' explanation has no code basis: close_segment_on_engine awaits without a deadline, and queue_reqs is 65,536 (shard.rs:1061).
- Post-split: rejections on P hit low-child appends.

How to confirm:
- DST_DRAIN_TRACE prints GATHER (gather.rs:230-243) and ADVANCE (maintenance.rs:159-168) lines.
- The product error body hides the message; use the raw surface body or tracing ('maintenance accounting diverged').

Plausibility: HIGHEST. It is the only steady-state Internal source found in this rig, but it is unproven.

items.name: RANK 2 — Shard-level maintenance apply_delta underflow (same root as rank 1)
items.where: src/shard/transaction/finalize.rs:25-31 → shard.rs:332-347 ('maintenance retirement exceeds backlog') → mod.rs:186-188 → 500
items.detail: The shard total is added minus retired. A double retirement from rank 1 larger than the whole shard backlog trips this, most likely when the engine drains to near zero (quiet gaps, seal time). The whole group gets Internal. Not committed (before db.write). Reachable wherever rank 1 is; sealing is the likeliest moment. Plausibility: medium, as a secondary manifestation of rank 1.

items.name: RANK 3 — SlateDB ErrorKind::Closed flattened to Internal (review item 47)
items.where: src/shard/transaction/finalize.rs:179-196 (db.write Err → reject; whole group); mod.rs:150-157 (stream_handle db.get error; per op); prepare.rs:53-84 → mod.rs:58-66 (billing meta read error; whole group); transaction/append.rs:36-45, 111-121 (producer/seq chain reads; per op)
items.detail:
Trigger: the shard DB closes under a live committer: fenced by a new writer, a SlateDB internal panic, or the window before the acker observes close_reason (shard.rs:3048-3060). The engine's own close cannot cause it, because storage-close runs only after workers are joined or aborted (tasks/shutdown.rs:56-80, shard/lifecycle.rs:53-74).

Phase reachability: a split never retires or reopens the parent engine (topology.rs:438-442, 465: the low child reuses the parent route) and the rig has no second writer. So it is unreachable in the capacity test, in any phase. Reachable in multi-instance ownership moves and fleet evictions — the production case.

Ambiguity: a db.write Err is usually not applied (slatedb check_closed runs before enqueue, db.rs:286/308), but a batch-writer death after enqueue is ambiguous. Read failures mean nothing was committed. Plausibility for this observation: very low.

items.name: RANK 4 — ResolveError::OpenFailed
items.where: application/append/submit.rs:18-25 → contract.rs:220-224 (Internal/ShardOpen) → 500 (raw 'shard_open'; product 'append_failed' retryable:false, product.rs:2421); sources: shard_directory.rs:296 ← sharddir.rs:542-553 (opener Err, including panics converted by sharddir/unwind.rs:38-44, e.g. the rig's `.expect("load maintenance")` at fixture_http.rs:287-289), :554-600 (open deadline, 180 s default), :621 ('open task vanished'); also application/append/close.rs:137-143 (sealed/sealing descriptors only)
items.detail: Trigger: the first resolve of a cold prefix whose open fails or panics, or a waiter still waiting at the open deadline. Phase reachability: 'children opening' — only when a customer append is the first to resolve a cold child prefix (production). In this test the child engine is opened by engine_for_scaler (topology_scaling.rs:392-399) before any child append and is never closed. ## Phases and how each pause is realized
No new production hooks. The rig uses prefixes 00/01/10/11, so the high child always gets its own engine. Keys: `gb` goes to the low child (parent's engine), `ga` and the raw empty key go to the high child.

| Phase | How it is held |
|---|---|
| intent | Phase A's exact descriptor state planted with `registry.cas_update`, then `scaler3::resume` |
| seal queued | `parent.test_hold_commit()`: 3 appends, then the close op, then 3 appends, all in one group; `appends_enqueued` proves each step arrived |
| seal written, not durable | FaultStore holds the WAL PUT; absorbers cold and paused; proof is `oldest_inflight_ms >= 50` |
| sealed, unpublished | `ScalerBeforePublish`; `parked() == 2` shows an append's resume is parked too. Variant: held past the 10 s request-work deadline |
| children opening | the rig's `open_park` holds the high child's first engine open past `open_wait` (10 s), then a later append joins the same open and it is released (proof: `open_stats` coalesced count) |
| parent engine retiring (queued) | commit gate held, then `shards.retire(prefix, FleetEviction)` |
| parent engine retiring (written) | WAL write held, retire, then release the store |
| stale cache | pre-split descriptor planted with `test_poison_cache` after publication |

There is no separate "published but cache not yet invalidated" window: the publication write already invalidates the registry cache.

## Outcome table
Every row was read back through the API, then retried with the exact same producer tuple and body.

| Phase | Low (`gb`) | High (`ga`) | Raw (empty key) |
|---|---|---|---|
| intent | 200, committed on parent, retry is a duplicate | 200, 1 copy, **retry makes 2 copies (F1)** | 200, **retry makes 2 copies (F1)** |
| seal queued, appends before the close | 200, retry duplicate | 200, **F1** | 200, **F1** |
| seal queued, appends after the close | 200, retried internally onto the child, 1 copy, retry duplicate | same | 200 then 204 duplicate |
| seal not durable | 200 once the close is durable, retry duplicate | same | same |
| sealed, unpublished (released) | 200 via the child, retry duplicate | same | same |
| sealed, unpublished (10 s) | 503 ra=1, nothing committed, retry 200 | same | 503 segment_transition ra=1, nothing committed, retry 200 |
| child opening, early appends | — | 503 ra=3, nothing committed, retry 200 | 503 shard_opening ra=3, same |
| child opening, late appends | 200 | 200, retry duplicate | — |
| retiring, queued | 503 ra=1, nothing committed, retry 200 (with or without producer tuple) | control 200 | control 200 |
| retiring, written | **503 ra=1 but committed (ambiguous)**; producer retry is a duplicate; bare retry makes 2 copies (F2) | — | — |
| stale cache | 200 via the child, retry duplicate | same | same |

The product surface shows all 503 codes (shard_moving, segment_transition, shard_opening) as `temporarily_unavailable`, with the Retry-After header kept.

Two notes on the harness itself:
- **Non-vacuity control:** failing the parent's commit group made all six seal-group appends answer 500 and failed the scenario. The failed close also made `execute_split` return false.
- **Phase B race:** in 2 of 70 loops the resume scheduled by the appends won Phase B instead of the split's own call. Nothing answered 500 and the appends before the close committed in both. So those two scenarios print which resume published instead of asserting it.

## Cause of the capacity-run 500
**Timing.** The failing run ended at 8.63 s. With window markers, the split starts at 8.64–8.92 s. So the panic surfaced at the end of the third pre-split window, not after the split.

**Causal path:**
1. Every 120 absorber ticks (2.4 s in this rig), the absorber rescans its dirty-stream index. If a gather's boundary advance is still queued in the committer, the rescan sees absorbed < mark, and `roll_back_stranded_mark` (`gather.rs:323-352`) drops the mark as stranded.
2. The next gather plans from the durable boundary (`plan_read`) and re-reads the in-flight range.
3. `CommitTransaction::absorbed` (`maintenance.rs:169-202`) retires the batch's full bytes whenever upto > prev, so the overlap is retired twice.
4. When the ledger then underflows, `finish()` rejects the whole commit group with "maintenance accounting diverged". Every append in that group answers Internal: product 500 `append_failed` (retryable:false), raw 500 `internal`. Nothing is written.

**Evidence:**
- One traced solo run shows the rollback at mark 1481 (durable 1455), then `GATHER from=1455`, then `ADVANCE prev=1481 upto=1502`, then four rejected groups at the catch-up after the load stopped.
- The same mechanism leaves a phantom backlog on the sealed parent. It also explains the "split executes" failures: when the seal's close shares a group with a diverging batch, the close is refused.

**Red regression (25 of 25 runs):** `a_rescan_during_an_inflight_advance_never_fails_an_append` (ignored) returns `Err(Internal("maintenance accounting diverged"))`. The control without the rescan, `a_regather_from_the_submitted_mark_retires_each_byte_once`, passes.

**Fix options for the owner** (all need your decision):
- bound each retirement to the advance's actual range;
- stop rolling back a mark while its batch may still be queued;
- drop a diverging maintenance op instead of failing the whole group.

## Other findings
- **F1, exactly-once broken across a split onto another engine.** `load_producer_chain` and `load_seq_chain` read lineage only from the serving engine's own database. The high child cannot see its parent's rows, so a producer retry commits twice, and a Stream-Seq below the parent's (0001 after 0002) answers 204 instead of 409. Two ignored red tests reproduce it:
  - `a_producer_retry_after_a_split_is_recognised_on_the_high_childs_engine`
  - `a_stream_seq_lane_after_a_split_refuses_a_regression_on_the_high_child`

  The existing `product_producer_hash_survives_split` only passes because it uses a one-prefix rig.
- **F2, ambiguous 503.** If the parent engine retires while its written group awaits durability, the group is answered 503 shard_moving ("retry"), but the record becomes durable. A retry without a producer tuple creates a duplicate.
- **Item 47 (Closed/Fenced store reported as 500):** not reachable in any single-instance split phase. Retirement answers `Moved`, which is 503. It needs a writer fence (ownership move).
- **Capacity test prefixes:** the test uses prefixes 00/01/02/03. Prefixes are matched against binary hash bits, so 02 and 03 never match and those hashes fall to the default "" prefix. The capacity split still lands on two engines, so the test still works.

## Load runs
20 runs of the diagnostic `post_split_throughput_scales` build (WARN/ERROR tracing, window markers, 500-body print), with two looping lib-suite processes running (load average 35–68):
- 20 of 20 passed, ratio 1.82–2.01, zero 500s.
- Every run rolled back an in-flight mark: 37 rollbacks, 18 of them in the third pre-split window.
- 10 of 20 runs logged the divergence (23 rejected groups). 4 of those happened during a load window: before-2 on the parent (runs 02 and 09) and after-3 on the high child (runs 07 and 16). No client append happened to share those groups, which fits a 500 appearing only rarely.

The diagnostic patch was not committed. Its binary, logs and analysis script are in the scratchpad at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sorenschmidt-code-streams/4580d18c-ad9e-4e38-8ca1-89558fd0d592/scratchpad/sbo-load/` (`capdiag`, `cap-01.log`…`cap-20.log`, `trace-0.log`, `analyze.py`, `runs.txt`). The commit messages are in the same scratchpad as `sbo-commit-a.txt` and `sbo-commit-b.txt`.
verdict:
**Verdict: the harness mostly holds up, but the release hold is not closable as submitted.**

The main conclusion is correct: the capacity-run 500 did not come from the split boundary. Four things stop closure:
- There is no fix. The reviewer's criterion is a causal fix plus a red regression.
- The red regression checks the symptom (a refused append), not the defect (bytes retired twice).
- The attribution is probable, not established.
- The headline "no split phase answers 500" is too broad: I produced a 500 at the split boundary.

**What I reproduced** (my own worktree at bc2907f7, now removed):
- The 9 phase scenarios pass.
- All three reds fail as described:
  - F1 producer retry: 200 and 2 copies.
  - F1 Stream-Seq: not 409.
  - Absorber: `Err(Internal("maintenance accounting diverged"))`.
- The absorber control passes.
- The builder's uncommitted non-vacuity control reproduces: all six seal-group appends answer 500 and the split returns false.
- My probes are saved as `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sorenschmidt-code-streams/4580d18c-ad9e-4e38-8ca1-89558fd0d592/scratchpad/skeptic-probes.patch`.

**(1) Do the pauses really hold the split?**

| Phase | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Seal queued | Proven by the control above. |
| Seal written but not durable, and retiring-written | The entry check is real. With no WAL hold, the longest in-flight wait over 5 s was 4 ms; the test requires at least 50 ms. |
| Sealed, unpublished (released) | The committed test only proves one shot reached the gap (`parked() >= 2`). My probe showed all 3 shots were queued on the parent in the gap, 8 of 8 runs. That should be asserted in the test. |
| Unpublished past 10 s, child opening, retiring-queued | Proven by the outcome: those 503 codes only arise in that state. |
| Stale cache | Weak. It proves the cache was stale before firing, but not that the append took the stale route. The outcome is the same either way. |
| Intent | By design, appends ignore a pending intent, so this is really "committed before the split, retried after it". It carries F1 but does not test a split phase. |

**(2) Phases missing from the reviewer's list**
- **Old-owner submission and redirect:** everything runs on one instance. Not tested: the redirect (409 `not_ring_owner` with `Streams-Replay-To`), `relay_segment_close`, and stale caches on other instances. The harness's `retryable()` would also flag a raw 409 `not_ring_owner` as a violation.
- **Handle retirement:** the harness retires the whole parent engine, which a single-instance split never does (the low child keeps that engine). Three things are not paused:
  - `scaler.retire_segments`;
  - eviction of the sealed parent's stream handle;
  - a retirement during `db.write` itself. The harness holds before the write and after it, not during it.
- **Publication:** not exercised:
  - a failed Phase B CAS (the `registry.fail_next_put` hook exists);
  - "split stays pending";
  - exhausting the 4-attempt `SegmentTransition` retry.

  The Phase B race was seen in 2 of 70 loops but is not controlled.
- **Maintenance divergence landing in the seal's group:** this is the builder's own explanation for the "split executes" failures (2 of 40 in `cap-tally.log`). It is not exercised at the split boundary, and there is no trace of a failing run.

**(3) Are outcomes read back?**
- Yes: every row is read back through a durable drain before and after the retry.
- But "committed on parent", "retried internally onto the child" and "via the child" are inferred. The `lands` column prints where the key routes now, not which segment holds the record.
- `Row::verdict` accepts "AMBIGUOUS: refused but committed" whenever a producer retry is reported as a duplicate. So the producer variant of F2 passes silently, and so would any 429 or 503 that actually committed. Only a 408 `append_timeout` is legitimately ambiguous.

**(4) The 500-path map.** These are all the append-path sources of HTTP 500:

| Source | Tested? | Reachable in the capacity test? |
|---|---|---|
| Registry read error in `prepare()` (`append.rs:80-87`) | No, and it is a real split-boundary 500 (see below). | No |
| `ResolveError::OpenFailed` (`contract.rs:220`), a reviewer-named suspect | No. There is no hook for a failing open, and the report never mentions it. | No: the test opens both children through `engine_for_scaler` before restarting load. In production it can hit the first append to a new high child. |
| `db.write` error (`finalize.rs:196`, item 47) | No. | No. "Needs a writer fence" is plausible from the code: shutdown aborts the committer after a 5 s grace, so the client gets 408, not 500. |
| Maintenance divergence (`finalize.rs:6` and `:28`) | Engine-level red only, no HTTP reproduction. | Yes |
| `billing_rows`, `stream_handle`, `load_producer_chain` / `load_seq_chain` errors; product handler's own registry read (`product.rs:~2098`) | No. | Only with store faults |

The registry-read gap: I armed `fail_next_get` while publication was held. The retry after the closed refusal re-runs `prepare`, and in 8 of 8 runs one shot answered 500 (product `append_failed` with `retryable:false`, raw `internal` "injected registry get failure"). `closure_is_current` answers 503 for the same failure one step earlier. Any transient store read error during a split can trigger this.

With a fault-free store, maintenance divergence is the only one of these sources reachable in the capacity run. That elimination supports the attribution; the report should state it.

**Capacity-500 attribution**
- **Timing: conclusion right, numbers wrong.**
  - In `cap-01` to `cap-20` the split starts at 8.598–8.742 s, not 8.64–8.92 s (8.921 comes from `trace-0` only).
  - There were 16 rollbacks in the third pre-split window, not 18.
  - The sound argument: no post-split window can end before about 9.7 s. Also, the test joins all clients before `execute_split` and opens both children before restarting load, so no client append can overlap any split phase in that test.
- **Mechanism: confirmed in code.**
  - `maintenance.rs` retires the batch's full bytes whenever upto > prev.
  - `finish()` rejects the whole group.
  - The absorber's advance batch shares the committer channel with client appends.

  But no client 500 was seen in the 20 loaded runs, and the original 500's body was never captured. Call it "probable, not established", the same standard the reviewer applied to F-G.
- **The red regression checks the symptom only.** I queued 10 appends between the two advances. All 10 succeeded, so the red's assertion would pass, but the ledger ended at 930 bytes against 1550 in the control: 4 frames of 155 bytes retired twice. So fix option 3 ("drop the diverging op") would turn the red green and leave the ledger silently corrupt. The control named `..._retires_each_byte_once` never checks bytes. Both tests need exact assertions on `applied.unabsorbed_bytes` and the shard's maintenance ledger.
- **The red only covers one interleaving.** It holds G1 in the committer queue. The builder's own `trace-0` logs the advance (1455→1481) before the rollback warning: G1 was already applied when the rollback ran, because the rescan's snapshot was older than the write. `plan_read` then starts from the durable boundary, which G1 had not reached yet. A fix that only skips rollback while the batch is still queued would pass the red and miss the traced case. It needs a second red: stale scan snapshot, G1 written but not durable.

**F1 and F2 are real.**
- **F1** is confirmed in code: `load_producer_chain` (`shard.rs:2043-2056`) reads only `self.db`. It hits every split in any topology with two or more prefixes, for keys in the high half, in any phase. It breaks exactly-once on its own and arguably blocks the release by itself.
- **F2**'s producer variant passes the verdict silently, as noted in (3).

Also confirmed: the builder's two commits change no production code.
